Job Description The Environmental Technicians will assist Idaho Power Company biologists with a population survey of white sturgeon in the Hells Canyon reach of the Snake River, the deepest gorge in North America. Techs will be part of 3-person, supervised field crews, deploying setline gear to capture white sturgeon between Hells Canyon and Lower Granite dams and a portion of the lower Salmon River, recording various fish metrics to assess population demographics. Work will be conducted from jet boats, piloted by experienced drivers, and often occur in high velocity current. Work shifts will initiate at Lewiston, ID., traveling by boat to sample sites, and at times traveling up to 100 miles when working in upper areas. Sampling will be conducted over a 3-day period beginning Tuesday am and ending Thursday pm during each survey week. Hours per week will vary, up to 35 hours approximate, depending on survey week. Work days up to 10 hours per day common; occasionally work days could exceed 12 hours, depending on sampling conditions. Overnight stays (2 nights) required when sampling upstream of Lewiston. Accommodations for lodging and meals will be provided when work shifts require overnight stays. No housing or relocation benefits will be provided for these positions.
Requirements: Required Skills Knowledge of: Working outdoors, accustom to working aboard boats in riveine environments useful. Prefer prior experience with fisheries data collection or other related biological disciplines. Skills in: Possess skills to follow detailed study protocol and operate field equipment with proper training and guidance. Work as part of a team with effective interpersonal and communication skills, strong work ethic and commitment to team success. Ability to: Perform physically demanding labor for extended periods of time and occasionally under adverse weather conditions, build effective working relationships, and positively represent the company when interacting with a wide variety and diverse group of people that frequent/use the Snake River. Required Experience MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS Education High school diploma or GED. Prefer associates degree in a related natural sciences discipline. PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS Job requires the person to occasionally bend, stoop, squat, crouch, climb into and out of vehicles/boats, twist, kneel, balance, reach, and commonly walk on uneven and rocky shoreline terrain. Requires sitting in a boat for extended periods of time while traveling to and from locations. Ability to function onboard a boat in rough water or high velocity current. Job requires the ability to occasionally lift items weighing up to 50 lbs. shoulder high and above, 75 lbs. waist high and knee high. Occasionally use exertional force up to 50 lbs. to push/pull items; occasionally carry items weighing up to 50 lbs. with two hands; frequently carry items weighing up to 15 lbs. with one hand. Must be able to firmly grasp 5/16 inch braided nylon rope to retrieve setlines, hold simple tools, various types of portable electronic equipment; use fine motor skills to write, operate a computer keyboard and use small hand instruments. Applicant must be able to perform the essential functions of the job without posing a direct threat of harm to self, others or property. Job placement is contingent upon successful completion of a pre-employment post-offer Functional Capacity Assessment (FCA). In addition, temporary/non-regular employees may contribute to the company sponsored 401k program upon hire, with the company match vesting after completing 12 continuous months of employment. Temporary/non-regular employees are only eligible to apply for internal job postings if the posting is in their current department and in their current job classification.
